operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case table names: "directors", "actors", "movies", "movies2actors", "movies2directors", "u2base" quoted; users unquoted lowercase — keep original spelling, quote all.
Column names mixed case: isEnglish, u_gender, a_gender, d_quality, a_quality, avg_revenue, cast_num, runningtime — case-insensitive lookup needed.
u2base is huge (996159 rows) > max_rows_per_table 300000: rowid%k sampling required; original_sizes must still be full count(*).
movies2actors 138349 rows also near cap; actors 98690.
FKs declared inline via 'references movies' with no explicit parent column -> pragma parent col NULL -> same-name child column (movieid/actorid/userid/directorid).
Composite PKs: movies2actors(movieid,actorid), movies2directors(movieid,directorid), u2base(userid,movieid) — composite-PK members get max_l0=30.
No self-references; no dangling FKs; all parents exist and are unique PKs.
Two indexes on directors (avg_revenue, d_quality) — must be recreated in empty clone; no views/triggers.
Declared TEXT columns store numeric-looking strings: age ('1','56','25'), occupation ('2','3','4','1','5'), rating ('1','2','3') — String fuzzer will treat as int-like and add +-1 variants.
year INTEGER but only 4 distinct values (1..4) — Number fuzzer with tiny element set; not a real year.
isEnglish TEXT with 'T'/'F' (not bool type) -> String fuzzer, not Bool.
u2base.userid distinct 1233 < users 6039 and movieid distinct 3424 < movies 3832: FK child columns are sparse subsets of parents (not all parents referenced).
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on all INTEGER columns: range [-10^0,10^0]=[-1,1] default scale 0 -> tiny ints, then +-1/+-2 perturbation; PKs get fresh draws (max_l0=inf) so userid/movieid/actorid/directorid become small random ints, not the original large ids.

String fuzzer on age/occupation/rating: elements are int-like strings so adds str(i+1),str(i-1); fresh strings from charset a-zA-Z 0-9() length 0..20 -> implausible values (FN risk: queries filtering age='25' or rating='3' may match by luck but mostly miss).

String fuzzer on u_gender/a_gender/isEnglish/country/genre: 5 original samples + pool literals, p=0.2 fresh random strings + 0.5 contaminate -> many garbage values; low-cardinality columns (2-9 distinct) get diluted -> FN on equality filters, FP on 'not in' style.
year INTEGER with 4 distinct values: Number list range quirk (list_max overwritten to full max) -> mostly fresh small ints, rarely 1..4 -> queries on year=1..4 mostly miss.

FK consistency: movies2actors.movieid drawn from movies.movieid final values, actorid from actors.actorid; u2base.userid from users.userid, movieid from movies.movieid — joins preserved, but since parents are small random ints, join cardinalities differ from original.
Composite PK dedup (sample_fresh_primary_keys) drops duplicate (movieid,actorid) rows -> movies2actors shrinks; u2base similarly.

Table sizes: choose_table_sizes gives 30..230 or level-based (level0=1+30u, x4 per level capped 2500) -> u2base/movies2actors may be much smaller than original 996k/138k -> FN on aggregate/count queries expecting large results.
No NOT NULL/CHECK enforcement in Python; all columns notnull=1 so NULLs unlikely but String fuzzer can emit empty strings.
No unique single-column constraints besides PKs -> drop_unique_duplicates no-op here.
Missing ties/duplicates: original u2base has 1233 users x 3424 movies sparse; TS random instance may create denser or sparser coverage -> FP/FN on 'users who rated >= N movies' style queries.
No Date/Time/Bool columns -> those fuzzers unused; no crash-fallback types.
